items.title: Production BrowserBroker grants and delegated bearer forwarding (unblocks every browser path)
items.summary: Give the Model Plane BrowserBroker a durable (Postgres) grant store and a production issue/acquire/revoke path. The gateway obtains a user-session grant when it creates a browser session, sends grant_id on POST /v1/agent/runs, forwards x-browser-authorization and x-inference-authorization, and derives child grants for AI runs instead of the interim session:{id} string. Add one end-to-end contract test (gateway -> model-gateway -> execution-core -> quarry-edge) in prod mode that fails on 401/403.
items.whyItMatters: Prod-mode Quarry requires a broker grant on every agent run and refuses to boot without a validator (SRC), yet nothing outside tests issues grants and the broker store is in memory (SRC). Until this lands, the in-app browser, the AI step/loop, co-browsing, the credential bridge, budgets carried in the grant and per-origin consent cannot work in production (INF, high confidence, not runtime-tested). This is the single highest-leverage item in the audit.

items.title: Gate Evaluate and raw script actions behind a grant capability and one-shot approval
items.summary: Make AgentAction::Evaluate (and raw CSS selector paths) read-only by default: run in an isolated world with a non-mutating document proxy, JSON-only arguments and credential-field masking. Mutating script requires an explicit grant capability plus a one-shot approval, and the planner does not see Evaluate unless the grant allows it.
items.whyItMatters: Quarry otherwise fails closed, but Evaluate has no approval branch, so any risky action (submit, delete, read a sensitive field) can be expressed as script and bypass the risk-classified approval model. The executor must be sound regardless of which caller reaches /step.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (CA018, CI114: three gates plus a domain allowlist for raw CDP; read-only isolated-world evaluate wrapper that cannot mutate the DOM)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 3 sources (Codex); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Evaluate runs in Page.createIsolatedWorld against a frozen read-only proxy of document (no setters, no event dispatch), JSON-serializable args only, credential inputs masked. Raw CDP only when the grant has rawCdp=true and the method is on an allowlist; request/cookie params that carry URLs are authorised.

verevonToday.gap: The Verevon UI facade refuses raw script, but Quarry accepts Evaluate{script} on normal runs: sensitive_approval_for_action handles dialog, upload and download only, and Evaluate appears in agent_routes.rs just as a label mapping (SRC, this audit). The execution-core LLM planner schema does not emit evaluate today (llm_planner.rs:53-65), so current exposure is via direct /step callers, compiled procedures and any future code-mode.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-browser, quarry-runtime, quarry-edge): isolated-world read-only evaluate by default; add 'evaluate_mutating' as a sensitive action needing a grant capability and one-shot approval (the same mechanism as upload/download). Model Plane: hide the action from the planner unless the grant allows it. Audit existing callers of Evaluate first.
items.risks: Some extraction flows may rely on mutating evaluate; audit callers before tightening.

items.title: Close the gateway search-cache ZDR and tenant hole, then publish a per-feature ZDR capability matrix
items.summary: Phase 1 (S): the gateway /search cache key (search.rs:218-226) holds query, limit, include_answer and filters but no org or user scope, and store() runs without any ZDR check (SRC, re-read in this T2 pass); results are kept 4 h and served stale when Quarry fails. Add the authorized org id to the key, skip lookup and store for ZDR requests and ZDR orgs, and route every cache through one shared should_cache() admission rule (never cache ZDR, credentialed, action or profile requests). Phase 2 (M): declare a per-feature ZDR capability matrix with explicit refusal codes, and keep a content-free ZDR run tombstone with a default retention janitor.
items.whyItMatters: Two architecture rules are broken at once: ZDR must propagate, and no tenant may see another tenant's data. If smart-router results include org-scoped corpus or Data Plane vector hits (INF from the router design, not traced end to end), this is a cross-tenant disclosure, not only a ZDR gap. Phase 1 is a one-file fix.

items.title: ZDR-safe telemetry: span sampler, late-ZDR registry, log filter and safe/sensitive log fields in Quarry and the gateway
items.summary: In quarry-edge telemetry.rs add an OpenTelemetry sampler and span processor that drop spans for zdr=true requests (plus a bounded registry for runs that turn ZDR after a span started) and a tracing Layer that keeps events emitted inside ZDR spans out of the JSON fmt layer. Add one small shared helper (Rust crate plus the quarryotel Go package) whose log API forces two maps, safe (ids, enum outcomes, durations, counts) and sensitive (url, query, error text, selectors), with export sinks stripping sensitive by default. Propagate ZDR posture on internal hops as a header and NATS header, and add an operator kill switch that disables all exporters.
items.whyItMatters: Architecture rule: Zero-Data-Retention must propagate. It currently stops at the observability boundary: telemetry.rs always installs a JSON fmt layer and an OTLP layer with no ZDR awareness, and change_routes.rs logs the source URL inside the very branch that says ZDR is active. A leak in logs or OTLP is invisible to users and would breach ZDR contracts, and it blocks safe SIEM export and support diagnostics.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (ZeroDataRetentionSampler returning NOT_RECORD, bounded late-ZDR trace registry, ZDR log-metadata filter, X-Zero-Data-Retention header honoured by helper services)
others: Codex in-app browser (every lifecycle log entry is {safe, sensitive} with stable prefixes; BROWSER_USE_DISABLE_AMBIENT_NETWORK kill switch)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources for ZDR-aware telemetry and 2 of 4 for privacy-classified logs; differentiator (Firecrawl-only for the sampler and registry)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rust: a custom opentelemetry Sampler returning Drop when parent context or attributes carry zdr=true; a bounded LRU of trace ids flagged ZDR after start, checked in a SpanProcessor on_end so descendants and in-flight spans are dropped; a tracing Layer that suppresses events inside zdr=true spans; a log helper with signature log(safe: Map, sensitive: Map) where sinks drop or hash sensitive and ZDR requests always drop it. Posture travels as an internal header (for example x-verevon-zdr) and a NATS header so receivers skip request-correlated logs. A QUARRY_DISABLE_AMBIENT_TELEMETRY switch turns off every exporter.

verevonToday.gap: ZDR is carried on requests, events (emit_for_zdr) and artifact paths, but telemetry.rs installs the JSON fmt layer and the OTLP layer unconditionally with no ZDR sampler or filter (no "zdr" string in telemetry.rs or quarryotel). Logging relies on a documented convention of low-cardinality fields; about 295 tracing macro calls exist across the crates and several carry error text or URLs (change_routes.rs:635 logs url inside the ZDR-active branch at debug level; default filter is info, so it only surfaces with RUST_LOG=debug). No cross-plane ZDR telemetry header exists.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane first. quarry-edge/src/telemetry.rs: add ZdrSampler, a ZDR trace registry plus SpanProcessor, and a ZDR-aware tracing Layer; create a shared obs module (Rust) mirrored in pkg/quarryotel (Go) exposing safe/sensitive helpers; add the ZDR propagation header to the cross-plane contracts folder next to cross-plane-token-requests.json. Then Model Plane (execution-core, model-gateway) and the Frontend Plane gateway adopt the helper. Keep content-free counters (outcome, duration, driver) outside the ZDR filter so ZDR tenants still have operational metrics. Add a test that a ZDR scrape and a ZDR browser step export zero spans and no log line containing the URL, and a lint that url/query fields are only logged as sensitive.

items.title: One strict ScrapeOptions contract: formats[], inline return (the ZDR path) and main-content controls
items.summary: Define ScrapeOptions once in quarry-core (deny_unknown_fields, validate() with field paths, schemars JSON Schema for OpenAPI and the Model Plane tool schema) with formats[] (markdown, html, rawHtml, links, metadata now; json, screenshot and pdf via F-t2-019 and F-t2-023), inline return up to a size cap with artifact-ref fallback, timeout, maxAge, onlyMainContent, include/exclude selectors, extractor choice (readability, clean_full, raw) with a full-HTML fallback, headers and location. Return effectiveOptions and a scrape_id, add GET /v1/scrape/:id (not for ZDR), and embed the struct in crawl, batch, search hydration and schedules.
items.whyItMatters: Every agent web_fetch pays two calls today (scrape, then GET artifact), and a ZDR scrape returns no content because outputs exist only as artifact refs that are never written under ZDR (SRC). Inline return is the natural ZDR path. One validated contract is what lets the Model propose options and Quarry reject bad ones with field-level 400s. docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:22 claims format parity is done; the code contradicts it (no formats field on ScrapeRequest).

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Validate the request against a single options schema; take a per-org concurrency permit with a bounded wait (2/3 of the request timeout); run the pipeline in-process; build the Document with only the requested formats (markdown default, rawHtml only on request) and put scrapeId, status code, final URL and queue time in metadata; cross-field rules (waitFor <= timeout/2, action count and total wait caps, one screenshot format); write a per-job access row {scrapeId, orgId, expiresAt} so GET /scrape/:id can re-serve the result, and write none for ZDR. Caution from the reference: it silently defaults skipTlsVerification to true, so echo effective options and never flip a security default silently. || Merged items add: Request: formats: Array<string | {type, ...opts}>; strings are lifted to {type} and validated against a tagged union so each format has its own option schema (serde #[serde(tag="type")] in Rust). Pipeline: fetch once, then run only requested transformers in a fixed order (clean html -> markdown -> links/images/attributes -> LLM formats -> redaction -> diff). Response: one Document with optional fields per format plus metadata {statusCode, sourceURL, url, contentType, cacheState, cachedAt, proxyUsed, creditsUsed, warnings[]}. Exclusive formats (raw base64) are rejected when combined with others. || Parse with a DOM or streaming rewriter (lol_html, kuchikiki). Remove head/meta/style/script/noscript. If includeTags is given keep only matching subtrees; remove excludeTags. If onlyMainContent, remove a fixed list of about 42 chrome selectors unless the node contains a force-include region. Resolve lazy images (data-src, data-srcset, largest srcset) against the base href. Choice of extractor, falling back to full cleaned HTML when readability yields too little text. Firecrawl's optional LLM clean pass is unsupported under ZDR and not worth copying.

items.title: Reap abandoned agent runs (idle and absolute TTL), cap concurrent runs, and make the fleet console real
items.summary: Add a background sweeper in quarry-edge that closes agent runs past their lease ttl_s (derived from max_runtime_s) or an idle timeout, releases the browser lease, emits a run.expired event and denies further use of the run's grant. Add per-org and global caps on concurrent runs and a tab-count warning, move the in-process run registry to durable state for multi-instance operation (non-ZDR only), and proxy /v1/fleets through the gateway so the fleet console shows real runs.
items.whyItMatters: Abandoned user or AI sessions currently hold a Chromium context and a live browser grant indefinitely. That is a resource leak on a shared browser host and a security exposure (a usable grant with no user present), and it grows with every agent run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (global run semaphore, sub-agent cap, tab warning, idle sweeper)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources; differentiator (only Aside has code evidence, and for a local single-user product)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A global semaphore (200 concurrent runs) gates run start; a per-run counter limits active sub-agents (8); the agent is warned at 5 open tabs; each tab carries a last-activity timestamp and a sweeper closes agent tabs and sessions past an idle TTL (15 minutes) and emits an event; ephemeral sessions are retained for a fixed 15-minute window.

verevonToday.gap: ttl_s is computed from max_runtime_s (default 120) and stored on the lease at agent_routes.rs:1446-1502 but nothing sweeps it; a grep of agent_routes.rs finds no idle or reaper logic. Only max_steps is enforced on the step path. Runs live in an in-process HashMap (new_runs) so they cannot be shared across edge instances. The lease pool holds 2 sessions on one shared Chromium. The fleet console is a stub with placeholder live views fetching /v1/fleets that the gateway does not proxy. Step budgets and fleet budget aggregation do exist.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane (quarry-edge) with a small Frontend change. items.title: Stop viewport-triggered browser relaunches: per-page emulation, a small Chromium process pool and page hygiene

items.title: Enforce cost and runtime budgets in the Quarry executor, meter browser time, and clamp crawls to the remaining entitlement
items.summary: The run contract carries max_cost_usd and max_runtime_s, but only max_steps is enforced on the /step path, defaults are unbounded and browser minutes are not metered (SRC). Quarry, as the executor, reserves on run start, charges per step and per browser-second, stops gracefully at the cap with a typed BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and clamps crawl/batch page limits and requests per minute to the remaining entitlement. Model Plane cost-core passes the remaining budget inside the grant and reconciles; org default caps arrive via the policy claims of F-t2-022.

items.title: Harden persistent browser profiles: complete snapshots, per-org envelope encryption at rest, ordered saves, ZDR enforced inside Quarry
items.summary: Capture cookie expiry, storage for every origin and IndexedDB in profile snapshots; envelope-encrypt snapshots (and secret job inputs) per org and owner with keys obtained through a Control Plane key API (env master key first, KMS later); add monotonic saved_at and deletion tombstones; wire the S3 store and the GDPR purge consumer; and enforce in Quarry, not only in the UI, that ZDR orgs get no persistent profile.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent profiles hold live session cookies for users' signed-in sites. Today snapshots are incomplete and not encrypted at rest (SRC), which is a data-governance risk that grows with every login handed to the agent. Encryption is specified in docs/CONTRACTS.md:185-199 but not implemented.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Profile = {id, scope, owner, fingerprint, egress affinity, snapshot blob ref, saved_at, deleted_at}. Save is an UPSERT with saved_at = GREATEST(saved_at, new) and is ignored when a newer deletion tombstone exists, so a late save cannot resurrect a deleted profile. Snapshot = all cookies (expiry, SameSite, partition key) + local/session storage per origin + IndexedDB export, encrypted with a per-org key. Profiles are refused under ZDR, lockdown and Safe Mode. Caller cookies go in with Network.setCookies at the registrable domain. || Merged items add: On save generate a random AES-256-GCM key, encrypt the value, wrap that key with an RSA-2048 public key unique to (user, tool) and persist ENCRYPTED_VALUE:<wrapped>:<ciphertext>. At run start the runtime receives the private key through a mounted file or env and decrypts in process; logs and stored input keep only ciphertext.

items.title: Org-pinned, tighten-only web policy: tri-state capability gates delivered as signed claims and enforced by Quarry
items.summary: Make the Control Plane the policy of record for web and browser capabilities (robots mode and override, maximum proxy tier, credential/cookie/header stripping, login or form-write actions for autonomous runs, raw evaluate, uploads and downloads, recording, persistent profiles, paid providers, domain allow/deny, ZDR) as disabled/allowed/forced, delivered on the signed-claim channel that already carries the ZDR floor and inside BrowserBroker grants as action classes. Quarry rejects at the edge and re-resolves per URL in PageRunner and the step path as a backstop. Requests, Spaces and the Model can only tighten.
items.whyItMatters: This is the direct implementation of three Verevon rules: Quarry executes or rejects, ZDR must propagate, and Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. Today two RunPolicy types exist and the edge hard-wires RunPolicy::default(), so no org or request policy is applied (SRC); control-plane presets are not consumed. Firecrawl Safe Mode (SRC) is the reference shape.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl Safe Mode (SRC)
others: Firecrawl (per-team tri-state flags and per-key restrictions), with Codex's default-off browser gates
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique, but it maps onto Verevon's own governance rules || 2 of 4 sources; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: ResolvedPolicy = merge(orgPolicy, defaults) is computed in the API layer, which rejects requests that ask for forbidden options (403 SAFE_MODE_BLOCKED), and is recomputed in the worker for every URL including crawl children as a backstop that downgrades instead of trusting the request. It strips Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization, write/press/executeJavascript actions, profiles and URL userinfo, blocks browser endpoints, and bypasses allow-listed domains. All violations produce audit events. || Merged items add: Firecrawl TeamFlags hold disabled|allowed|forced per capability (ZDR for scrape and search can be forced, plus ignoreRobots, threatProtection, ipWhitelist); effective option = forced ? on : (allowed ? request : reject with typed error). Keys additionally carry allowedEndpoints and allowedFormats, checked per request and cached about 60 s. Codex keeps fine-grained gates (browserUse, full CDP access, webMcp, record-and-replay, auto-auth-for-sites, multi-window) that default to off with a dev-only env override.

Then Control Plane org-core policy storage and admin UI, auth-core claim minting, BrowserBroker action-class grants, and Quarry edge/PageRunner enforcement with typed denials (F-t2-032 builds per-origin consent on top). || Source detail: [R-t2-04-05] Control Plane: org policy record, entitlements (robots.ignore, proxy.enhanced, and so on) and audit events. Enforce at the edge by rejecting with a typed sub-code, and again in PageRunner and agent step execution per URL (including crawl children and redirects), downgrading rather than trusting the request. Remove or entitlement-gate presets that contradict governance (fast = RobotsIgnore, stealth). Model Plane: pass the resolved policy in the run grant so the planner does not propose forbidden actions. Model Plane: browser-broker adds allowed_action_classes and allowed_formats to ordinary grants (persisted in Postgres or Redis), computed from the org policy intersected with capability-core's Allow/Deny/Ask decision, with escalation through the existing approval flow. Quarry: the grant validator checks action class per step; ship default-deny plus sensitive approval for Evaluate immediately, independent of the rest.

items.title: Per-org capacity: concurrency caps with backlog and fair share, per-class rate limits and plan-aware quotas
items.summary: Add a per-org concurrency cap with a bounded backlog and fair-share priority inside the existing Postgres queue (Firecrawl pattern: over-limit work waits with an expiry, 429 only when the backlog is full), per-endpoint-class rate limits on the gateway browser, scrape and search routes, and plan-keyed limits read from Control Plane entitlements via claims (no cross-plane DB reads).
items.whyItMatters: With a two-session lease pool and no per-org caps, one tenant can starve all others; the browser, search and ingestion gateway routes have no rate limiting (SRC per baseline). Plan-scaled limits are table-stakes for web platforms (Firecrawl SRC, Apify DOC).

others: Firecrawl (SRC)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Sync path: a per-tenant lease semaphore (holders with TTL, heartbeated) waits up to 2/3 of the request timeout with jittered backoff. Async path: if active(org) >= limit, insert into backlog(org, job, times_out_at) instead of the queue; when a job finishes, promote the oldest backlog entry respecting per-crawl max concurrency; a reaper expires backlog rows (max 48 h). Backlog capacity = clamp(limit x 2000, 50k, 2M); overflow returns 429 naming the limit. Fair share: priority stays at base until in_flight(org, 60 s window) exceeds a bucket limit, then base + ceil((count - bucketLimit) x planModifier). || Merged items add: A Redis limiter keyed by (org, endpoint class). Limit = base[class] x plan multiplier, with per-org overrides. Cheap status polling has a high limit and browser sessions a low one. The limiter fails open if the entitlement lookup is down, and returns 429 with Retry-After. || BASE_RATE_LIMITS per endpoint class (scrape 10, map 10, crawl 2, search 10, extract 2, browser 2, status 500 per minute) multiplied by a plan multiplier (1, 10, 50, 500), with per-org overrides per mode; a token-bucket limiter keyed by (org, mode); priority tier derived from the same multiplier. Quotas are counted on create (schedules, webhooks) and rejected with a typed error.

items.title: Per-operation browser deadlines, bounded tab attach and retry-once on a destroyed execution context
items.summary: Give every CDP operation in quarry-browser an explicit deadline from one constants table (command, page-ready, capture, accessibility quiet window, tab attach), wrapped by a single helper that returns a typed Timeout with the operation name. Add one retry for lightweight calls that fail with a destroyed execution context (re-resolving the context first), and never replay coordinate actions after state changed. Make the table overridable per run policy.
items.whyItMatters: Hung or flaky browser steps are the first thing users watching the live view and agents will notice, and they waste Model steps on transport errors. The fix is small and has a clear reference design.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (SRC)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources has a per-operation table (Codex); every reference bounds work in some form, so the capability is common even though the table is unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A constants table of deadlines wrapped around every CDP call (about 20 s per command, 15 s page-ready, 1.5 s cursor, 5 s capture, 750 ms accessibility quiet cap), with debugger leases cleaned up on timeout. A pending-open map resolves when a tab attaches or rejects after a 15 s handshake with distinct failure causes. DOM operations cache an isolated world per (target, frame, loader); on a context-destroyed error the cache is dropped and the call is retried once. Semantic errors are never retried.

items.title: Honest bot-block handling: closed block taxonomy, non-signals, one recovery, a user-visible blocked state, and no stealth code
items.summary: Split outcomes into strong bot-block signals (captcha, WAF interstitial, challenge loop) and non-signals (bare 403/429, timeouts, sign-in or paywall pages, region blocks). Add a closed BlockReason enum with hostname-only aggregated telemetry, give the browser planner an explicit rule (at most one low-risk recovery such as a short wait and one reload, then stop, tell the user and switch source), and render a 'site blocked automated access' state with take-over and try-another-source actions in the Verevon browser. Delete the unused stealth scripts and the vestigial stealth_level plumbing.
items.whyItMatters: Users and agents get a truthful, consistent result when a site blocks automation, and enterprise buyers get a defensible no-evasion posture that fits 'Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects'. Hostname-only counters are ZDR-safe and can feed the later domain registry. The dead stealth code currently contradicts the stance.

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 4 sources (Codex, Apify); differentiator, and the one that matches Verevon's governance stance
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A classifier reads site-served evidence (URL, DOM markers of Cloudflare/Akamai/hCaptcha/Turnstile, a fresh screenshot) and outputs {kind, confidence, evidence}. Strong signals versus non-signals are defined explicitly: bare 403/429, timeouts, sign-in pages, paywalls and region blocks are not bot detection. At most one recovery (short wait, single reload), no fingerprint or network changes, then stop and tell the user. A closed-reason report (captcha_failed, access_denied, challenge_loop, unexpected_bot_error) records only the hostname.

Missing: explicit non-signal rules (the host scheduler lumps 401/403/451/999/CDN-challenge into one Blocked bucket), a closed report taxonomy with hostname-only telemetry, planner text for the one-recovery rule, and a user-facing blocked state. stealth.rs (STEALTH_SCRIPT and an auto-accept CONSENT_DISMISS_SCRIPT) has no caller outside its own file, and DriverPlan.stealth_level is set (0/1/2) but never read outside driver_plan.rs, so the code contradicts the stance and one baseline narrative wrongly describes it as active.

items.title: Quarry /metrics recorder, per-run statistics and graceful drain, then a span vocabulary, memory-aware admission and alert rules
items.summary: Phase 1 (S, ship first): install the metrics-exporter-prometheus recorder in quarry-edge, serve /metrics on an internal-only port with about 20 low-cardinality series (queue depth, browser pool active/idle/launch latency, driver outcome by driver and outcome, egress broker health, cache hit/miss, webhook delivery), and persist a RunStatistics object on the run row (finished/failed/retried, retry histogram, status-code counts, top error signatures). Phase 2: infrastructure alert rules on the existing Control Plane Prometheus, plus user-facing run-failure and data-quality alert rules in quarry-control delivered through notification-core. Phase 3, after item 01: a span vocabulary (browser.<action> with url.origin, driver, outcome, snapshot bytes; scrape.pipeline with engine attempted/winner and cache state) with approval wait excluded from agent latency, and W3C traceparent propagation gateway to execution-core to Quarry. || Install a Prometheus recorder and serve /metrics on quarry-edge with low-cardinality queue depth, lease pool, per-org active runs and step latency; add SIGTERM drain to edge and the orchestrator worker. Then wrap the browser lease pool with the existing AutoscaledPool driven by cgroup memory and Chromium RSS, refusing leases above a threshold with a typed RESOURCE_BUSY the Model Plane can retry, and report the host unhealthy after repeated refusals.
items.whyItMatters: Quarry has no metrics, so there are no SLOs, capacity planning or alerts for the browser and crawl layer that users and agents depend on, and scheduled monitors can break silently. Latency attribution across gateway, Model and Quarry is how slow or failing agent runs get debugged. || Autoscaling, admission and the reaper all need real numbers. items.title: Monitor change quality: normalised-content fingerprint, text/JSON diffs, tags and an optional goal-aware judge
items.summary: Phase 1 (priority): compare a fingerprint of normalised main-content markdown instead of the raw response bytes, return a paragraph diff from /v1/change/check using the unused diff_paragraphs, accept a tag so one URL can keep separate histories, and add an optional schema-based JSON diff. Phase 2 (recommended, needs the model grant): a Model Plane judge reads the diff and the monitor's stated goal and returns {meaningful, confidence, reason, changes[]}; alerts fire when meaningful or when the judge fails (fail open).
items.whyItMatters: Monitoring already ships in the Verevon UI, so noise (ads, timestamps flagged as change) and the absence of any diff are visible to users now. A goal-aware verdict turns monitors into an agent-grade feature and cuts notification noise in the Application Plane.

items.title: Approval loop UX: keyboard-first approval card with redirect, persisted site rules and attention notifications
items.summary: Extend the existing browser approval gate into a full loop. Model Plane owns the approval schema (risk level, display-friendly params, origin, page URL, persist session|always) and persisted per-user or per-org host rules stored as BrowserBroker policy, never widened through Spaces. items.title: Durable hosted browser sessions: idle and absolute TTLs, suspend/resume, view vs control tokens, optional recording, scrape-to-session replay
items.summary: Move agent browser run state from the in-process run map to a durable session store with a state machine (starting, running, suspended, stopped, failed), idempotent create, separate idle and absolute TTLs instead of the fixed 120 s / 12 step UI defaults, and suspend/resume implemented as a profile snapshot plus browser release and restore. Issue separate read-only and interactive live-view tokens and add optional recording gated by org policy (off under ZDR). As a later phase, persist a ReplayContext (url, actions, profile, location) on scrape results and add POST /v1/scrape/:id/session so a user or a Model run can continue from a scrape result.
items.whyItMatters: Two minutes is short for real browsing, an in-process map loses runs on restart, and enterprises want audit recordings. The plan documents say crash-safe resume is not yet proven for every provider, and 'continue interactively from this scrape' is a natural AI-first flow.

items.title: Durable, tenant-scoped authority and one audit record for every permission and approval decision
items.summary: Persist BrowserBroker grants (today an in-memory map), add a production issuance path and scope inheritance for child runs and fleets, and put evaluate and raw-CSS actions behind a sensitive one-shot grant. Add org_id to the quarry-control Webhook model, front webhook CRUD through edge with JWT org scoping, and add a dispatch-id header, a test endpoint and a longer retry ladder. Define an AuthzDecision event in audit-core (schema_version, permission, decision, decision_context, a decided_by enum separating user, saved, policy, reviewer and system, policy_id, reason_code, origin only, run_id, actor_id, duration_ms) that execution-core approvals, browser-broker validations and Quarry policy denials publish to verevon.audit.v2.*; record only denials for high-volume per-navigation checks.
items.whyItMatters: It keeps the authority model credible (Quarry executes only what a grant allows and scope cannot widen through child runs or webhooks) and completes the evidence chain for "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects", which enterprise compliance reviews ask for. Without tenant-scoped webhooks, crawl and monitor webhooks cannot be exposed to customers.

others: Aside (read methods whitelisted; lifecycle mutations only through ownership-tracking tools)
Apify webhooks (11 retries over about 32 hours, dispatch-id header, test button, no HMAC)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grant = {principal, scopes[], allowed_domains[], budget, expires_at, parent_grant}; children inherit min(parent scopes) and escalation needs a recorded human approval. The component that decides emits AuthzDecision with an outcome enum {not_needed, policy_allowed, reviewer_approved, reviewer_denied, user_approved, user_approved_for_session, user_denied, user_aborted, timeout}. Webhooks are (org_id, url, secret, events), HMAC signed, retried with exponential backoff, DLQ at the end, registered only through edge.

items.title: Document parsing depth: PDF classification and Model Plane OCR routing, Office and e-book conversion, bounded parsing and a per-org parse cache
items.summary: Branch on PDF (content-type and %PDF magic) in the scrape/crawl pipeline: classify pages as text or scanned, extract text natively with the existing lopdf code, and route only pages that need OCR or layout to the Model Plane document-intelligence provider. Add parsers:[{type:pdf, mode: fast|auto|ocr, maxPages}], per-page markdown and optional layout blocks with bounding boxes, and reuse the same OCR path for raster image URLs. || Add a quarry-transform document module that detects DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODF, RTF, CSV and EPUB from bytes and converts them to markdown under zip-bomb and part-size budgets, branch to it by content-type in the scrape/crawl pipeline, and add a crawl option to follow and store linked office/PDF files as artifacts. Put resource governance around all document parsers (including the PDF path): a tokio semaphore, size ceilings, per-page time budgets, and a content-hash parse cache keyed per org and disabled under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise knowledge is mostly PDF; crawls that skip PDFs leave the Data Plane incomplete and answers ungrounded. The pieces exist in separate planes (native text extraction in Quarry, Azure prebuilt-layout in the Model Plane) but nothing connects them for a crawl. || Company sites link office documents and enterprise users expect them ingested into the Data Plane. referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Sniff content-type and bytes; classify per page (text-layer coverage, image area) into text, scanned, image or mixed with a confidence and pagesNeedingOcr; if text-based with high confidence convert natively with heading ranking; otherwise send only the pages needing OCR to an OCR/layout service and merge per page; emit markdown, optional pages[] and blocks[{type,label,bbox,content}]; mode fast fails with a typed OCR_REQUIRED error on scans. items.title: Agent presence and run control UX: animated cursor and target highlight, real annotation markers, steer/queue follow-ups, needs-attention notifications
items.summary: Build one overlay layer in BrowserChrome that maps Quarry AX-ref rects (scaled to the frame) onto the frame stream. items.title: Parallel batch scrape with shared options, idempotent creation and wait-or-resume
items.summary: Make /v1/batch fan out under a concurrency bound (min of maxConcurrency, the org limit and the per-host AIMD scheduler) with shared scrapeOptions, appendToId, an invalid-URL report and the shared status/errors/cancel routes. items.title: Sitemap, robots and index-assisted crawl discovery, plus URL canonicalisation and redirect de-duplication
items.summary: Extract the /v1/map sitemap code into a shared Rust discovery module that also reads robots.txt Sitemap lines, gzip sitemaps, scoped, root and registrable-domain sitemaps, and URLs already in the local index or tracked sources. Call it from crawl kickoff behind a sitemap include|only|skip option, seeding the durable frontier through the scope filter. In the same enqueue path add a canonical_url unique_key and a post-redirect check so the same page is not crawled twice.
items.whyItMatters: Docs and product sites are Verevon's main knowledge sources; sitemap seeding makes crawls complete and cheap, and reusing the local index makes re-crawls incremental. referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Kickoff scrapes the start page then queues sitemap jobs for every candidate in parallel (3 concurrent, 25 nested max): robots Sitemap lines, <scope dir>/sitemap.xml, /sitemap.xml and the registrable-domain sitemap (plus /sitemap.txt). It parses urlset versus sitemapindex, decompresses .gz, recurses to a cap, filters each URL through the same scope filter and enqueues at a lower priority than seed links. items.title: Fetch-path reliability: one deadline budget, wired retries and typed failure sub-codes
items.summary: Add timeout_ms to scrape and agent requests and split it across the FallbackDriver waterfall with child cancellation tokens (reserve a minimum slice for the final browser tier, map client disconnect to the root token). Wire the already-written execute_with_retry into PageRunner using ErrorCode::retryable(), with maxRetries on the policy and no retries for ChallengeDetected or SecurityBlocked. Add a sub-code and detail field on QuarryError (DNS, TLS, all drivers failed, robots-blocked, and a processing-continues detail for long jobs), versioned across Temporal, webhooks and the gateway.
items.whyItMatters: Escalation through the static, TLS and browser drivers should finish inside one user-visible deadline instead of timing out with nothing. Transient failures should be retried the same way on scrape, crawl and agent paths. The Model and UI need to know why a fetch failed so they can switch source, wait or ask the user, instead of seeing a generic DriverFailed.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Compose cancellation tokens: request token (client disconnect) to scrape deadline token to per-engine child tokens, so an engine timeout cancels only that engine and the waterfall continues, while a scrape timeout cancels everything. Queue waits get a fraction of the budget (2/3), waitFor is at most half the timeout, and defaults are computed from the requested features. One ErrorCode union with about 55 codes extends a transportable base with serialize/deserialize so code and details cross queues and webhooks unchanged; long jobs return a processing_continues detail with estimated remaining time. Retry: count per request, an error hook may change the request, then requeue with backoff until the retry cap, then a failure hook.

verevonToday.gap: execute_with_retry is exported but called only from its own tests; Temporal activity retries (5 attempts, exponential) and the FallbackDriver chain are the only live retry paths. Per the baseline, cancellation is a flat token, /v1/scrape exposes no request timeout and the waterfall has no per-driver budget (not re-checked here). quarry-core ErrorCode has 17 coarse codes with retryable() and http_status(); it has no fetch-level detail (DNS, TLS, all drivers failed, robots-blocked, cache miss) and no processing-continues contract, although api_error carries retry_after_seconds. Strict TLS everywhere is already the safe default (no accept-invalid-certs found).

items.approach: Ingestion Plane. (a) Deadlines: add timeout_ms to scrape and agent-run requests with defaults computed in one function from the requested features; build a child CancellationToken per driver attempt with remaining-budget accounting in FallbackDriver and a reserved minimum slice for the last driver; map axum client disconnect to the root token; keep strict TLS. (b) Retries: call execute_with_retry from PageRunner, take the cap from RunPolicy.retry (exists in the quarry-core contract), skip ChallengeDetected, SecurityBlocked and robots denials, and consult the AIMD host scheduler so retries cannot storm a blocked host. Share one reqwest retry middleware for edge-to-control and Model Plane calls. (c) Errors: add a sub_code plus details to QuarryError (for example DriverFailed{dns|tls|connect|all_drivers_failed}, Forbidden{robots|policy}) rather than exploding the top-level enum, as the improvements doc section 39 also advises; add a processing_continues detail for long jobs; propagate through Temporal activities, webhooks, the gateway's recoverable/unrecoverable classification and Model Plane tool results; version the error schema.
dependencies: F-t2-027 (BlockReason maps onto the same detail field)

items.title: Org-scoped URL cache with explicit freshness, and a cache-only no-egress mode
items.summary: Add a URL plus variant keyed cache in Ingestion Plane over the existing artifact storage (Postgres metadata, Redis hot path), keyed by org, with maxAge/minAge/store flags on scrape and agent fetches, cacheState and cachedAt in the output metadata, and negative caching. ZDR orgs bypass it entirely. In a second phase add a no_egress policy flag that pins the driver plan to cache and Data Plane artifacts and returns a typed miss without logging the URL.
items.whyItMatters: Repeated agent research becomes cheaper and faster, fewer requests hit target sites (which also reduces blocks), and the Model gets explicit freshness it can reason about. The no-egress mode gives regulated or sovereign workspaces a hard guarantee of no outbound traffic.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Firecrawl); unique, with lockdown as a further unique mode
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Key = hash(normalised URL) plus variant (mobile, country, stealth, blockAds, wait, screenshot options). Raw body goes to object storage, a metadata row to an index table, hot entries to a Redis LRU that fails fast. The read path resolves maxAge (explicit, then dynamic per domain via a 200 ms race, then a 2-day default), queries the newest entry in the window and returns cacheState hit/miss plus cachedAt; negative windows skip the DB on repeat misses and entries whose body is missing are deleted. Lockdown rewrites the engine plan to index-only, disables robots/sitemap/redirect fetching, forces ZDR and returns a typed cache-miss error that does not log the URL.

verevonToday.gap: The Quarry cache is keyed by content fingerprint and is read only when the caller sends prev_fingerprint (and never under ZDR), so there is no URL or maxAge cache, no cacheState metadata, no negative caching and no cache-only mode; SWR claimed in PRESETS.md is absent. The gateway has separate 4 h search and scrape-preview caches (see R-t2-04-02). Artifact storage and Data Plane document storage already exist as bodies to serve from.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: after R-t2-04-02 lands the shared should_cache(), build the URL index with org-scoped keys, store bodies in the existing artifact store, hot path in Redis, flags maxAge/minAge/store on scrape and agent observation fetches, cacheState and cachedAt in NormalizedOutput, negative cache for failures, self-healing when a body is missing. Phase 2: no_egress policy flag (carried by the org policy floor, R-t2-04-05) that pins DriverPlan to a cache/Data-Plane-artifact driver, calling Data Plane APIs rather than its database, and returns a typed miss error without logging the URL.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane; Data Plane for the artifact-backed no-egress path
items.risks: Cross-tenant leakage if keys are not org-scoped or authenticated content is cached; stale answers surprise users, so always show cachedAt. Lockdown value is limited to a niche of regulated orgs.

items.title: URL and domain reputation gate before fetch and navigation, then layered screening (reviewer model, Quarry-side injection labels)
items.summary: Add a ReputationProvider trait in quarry-security that SecurityEngine.preflight and the agent validate_navigation hook call before any fetch, redirect or discovered crawl link. Start with a local hash-prefix list (Web Risk Update-style) so full URLs never leave the platform, add per-org modes (off, normal, customer secure-web-gateway categories such as Zscaler) in Control Plane, and never persist verdicts for ZDR orgs. || Three optional defence-in-depth layers. Model Plane: a fixed-rubric, tool-less reviewer model that can pre-approve low-risk first-visit approvals (never hand-off or always-confirm tiers), fails closed, caches allow per (thread, origin) with a short TTL and logs decisions in receipts. Quarry scrape/extract: an opt-in prompt-injection flag that labels suspicious spans or fails with a typed error.
items.whyItMatters: Autonomous browsing can reach phishing or malware pages, and enterprise customers want their own secure-web-gateway policy applied to Verevon's agent traffic. validate_navigation already gates every Model-proposed navigation, so the hook exists and the feature is a strong enterprise-sales point. || Cuts approval fatigue and supports unattended scheduled runs, protects agents from phishing and injection farms, and gives direct Quarry API consumers the same guard the agent path already has.

items.summary: Persist compiled browser procedures (versioned, tagged, org and owner scoped), add an execute endpoint that replays a procedure through the normal step path with grant, approval and budget checks, and offer 'save as procedure' after a successful agent run. First add optional postcondition assertions to agent steps so typical click, type and select runs can reach Verified status, because the compiler today rejects anything unverified.
items.whyItMatters: Turning a one-off agent browsing session into a repeatable, schedulable procedure is the step from 'the agent browses' to 'the product automates', and a replay is cheaper than re-planning every run. Quarry already has the hard part (compile, replay-compare, quality and impact checks) which Firecrawl's open source does not expose.

Re-implement as: distill the verified action trajectory into a parameterized procedure (steps, element refs, input schema) plus a natural-language skill; store with a version; replay executes deterministic steps and hands drift back to the agent. Apify adds immutable builds numbered MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD, tag-to-build mapping and pinning, and records the resolved build on each run.

items.summary: Have the Model Plane send turn_id and parent_run_id on every proposed browser action. Quarry records them, supports tab marks (deliverable, handoff), exposes a turn_ended endpoint that the Model Plane calls on turn end, interrupt and sub-agent stop (closing unmarked agent-opened tabs, downloads and blobs), and lets child runs reuse the parent's browser context under the parent's grant with narrower budgets. || Extend Quarry's existing AgentRunCheckpoint, which today stores one current_url, page hash, constraints, viewport, zdr, grant id and control mode, with the full tab list (URL, title, a bounded history window, active tab, agent or user flag). Resume then means a new lease plus lazy tab restore, and reopening a chat thread shows its tabs. Add a live-page budget in the lease scheduler that protects the active, agent-controlled, loading and downloading tabs and evicts by inactivity, restoring from the checkpoint on demand. Nothing is persisted under ZDR.
items.whyItMatters: Deterministic cleanup at turn end is ZDR-friendly (no leftover pages or downloads) and keeps agent context small. Sub-agent sharing lets Model Plane multi-agent runs cooperate in one browser without duplicating grants. || A paused agent run or a HITL handoff can resume on the same pages, and idle Chromium pages stop costing money. It is also what makes co-browsing durable across a closed laptop.

items.title: Engine planner v2: declared capability matrix, typed re-plan signals with budgets, learned per-domain mode and a domain-intelligence registry
items.summary: Replace plan_from_signals's five booleans with a FeatureFlags set and a static per-driver capability matrix (reusing BrowserDriverCapabilities for browser drivers), so callers never name a driver and each plan can be explained in receipts. Let drivers and content checkers return a typed Replan {NeedsBrowser, NeedsStealth, IsFile, Drop(flag)} under a ScrapeBudget {max_attempts, per_flag_flips, deadline}, and make static-to-browser hedging an opt-in preset. Add a DomainRenderProfile store (host-level verdicts only, ZDR-safe) fed by FallbackDriver escalations and a 5-10 percent dual-run sampler on crawls, with operator approval before a learned verdict is promoted. || Build the planned per-domain registry in quarry-control and give it two first consumers. (1) Passive, non-ZDR learning of which driver (static, TLS, browser) works per domain, using deterministic text similarity in Rust, feeding DriverPlan. (2) A trusted site-guidance field (rate hints, playbooks, 'do not automate' notes) that Quarry attaches to observations as labelled trusted metadata for the Model, separate from page content.
items.whyItMatters: Today every request to a JS-only site pays a static attempt plus a hydration settle, and adding a stealth tier, remote provider, file parser or provider-API engine means editing branching code. A declared matrix and typed re-plan make cost and tail latency bounded and auditable, which fits Verevon's receipts-first design, and learned verdicts cut browser cost on large crawls. || Cheaper and faster crawls with fewer wasted browser launches and fewer block events, and a clean way to steer the Model with trusted site knowledge that does not come from the untrusted page, reducing prompt-injection exposure.

items.title: Scrape request context and egress tiers: locale/geo/mobile emulation, country egress with policy-gated auto-escalation, profile pinning and cache partitioning
items.summary: Add profile_id, location {country, languages} and a mobile/device preset to ScrapeRequest and to lease creation. When a profile is set, the planner must use only profile-capable browser drivers, never the static/TLS tiers, never read or write the scrape cache, and stamp the profile scope into receipts. Apply Emulation.setLocaleOverride, setTimezoneOverride, setGeolocationOverride, setDeviceMetricsOverride and setUserAgentOverride at context creation, tag proxy-pool entries with a country, and include (country, languages, mobile) in the cache key. || Extend ProxyPool and EgressBroker with a vendor-neutral tier (direct/first-party, basic datacenter, enhanced residential or mobile) and an optional country, exposed as proxy: auto|basic|enhanced and country on scrape and agent runs. The broker plans basic first and escalates to enhanced only on rate-limit, transport or region-block outcomes when org policy allows it. The Model never picks the proxy. In a second phase turn the in-memory (host, proxy) health into a SessionPool that scores identities (proxy, cookie jar, fingerprint) and retires bad ones.
items.whyItMatters: The UI is Norwegian-first, so localized pricing and content matter. Scraping behind a login is only safe for knowledge ingestion if personalised pages can never leak across tenants through a shared cache and if the content inherits the owner's ACL. || Higher success on geo-restricted and rate-limited public sites for both user browsing and agent research, and localized results for market-research use cases, without a per-request choice by the Model. Verevon currently has only a flat proxy list, no geo control in the gateway or UI, and no identity health beyond a 60 s cooldown.

Attempt 1 uses the basic pool. On a block signal (401/403/429 or a challenge hint) a typed 'needs stronger egress' error is caught by the waterfall, which retries once on the enhanced pool inside the same retry budget, with the timeout raised for stronger tiers. Pool choice is encoded as (group, country, sticky session id). Policy can pin the maximum tier per org (Safe Mode forces basic). A SessionPool holds N sessions (proxy session id, cookie jar, score): markGood decays the score, markBad raises it, a blocked status retires the session, and state persists across restarts.

Session health retirement is phase 2. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-05] Ingestion Plane: add profile_id, location and mobile to ScrapeRequest and BrowserLease; set profile_required internally (ignore the client `signals` value for it), reject static/TLS fallback and cache admission when set, record the profile scope in receipts; apply CDP overrides at context creation (uses the per-page emulation from R-t2-03-01); add country tags to QUARRY_PROXY_POOL entries and a PrivacyPolicy check for third-party proxy processors. Data Plane ingestion must give scraped authenticated content the owner's ACL. Frontend Plane: device/locale picker in BrowserChrome and pass the user's locale instead of the fixed viewport. || [R-t2-04-07] Ingestion Plane. Phase 1: add ProxyTier plus country tags to ProxyPool entries; add proxy and country fields to /v1/scrape, crawl and agent-run requests; EgressBroker plans basic first and escalates to enhanced only for 429, repeated transport failure or an explicit region-block signal, and only when the org policy floor (R-t2-04-05) allows enhanced; never escalate to get past a strong bot signal (R-t2-04-03, INF adaptation of Firecrawl's 401/403/429 trigger). Record tier and country in the existing redacted egress receipts and in usage so Control Plane can meter per-GB cost and entitlement. Every vendor stays a registered third-party processor under the PrivacyPolicy gate, and ZDR orgs may only use processors with ZDR terms. Phase 2: promote broker health to a SessionPool keyed (org, host-group) with EWMA error scores and retirement; keep it in memory for ZDR orgs and use Redis with TTL otherwise; keep agent-run affinity sticky and, when blocked mid-run, propose a choice to the user instead of silently rotating mid-login. items.title: Agent routines: scheduled, heartbeat and event-triggered agent runs with per-fire browser grants
items.summary: Let the agent create persistent routines through one confirmed tool: cron or one-shot runs in a new session, heartbeats that wake the same conversation later, and event routines fired by webhook, email or notification events. Build on the Model Plane's existing cron_schedules and fire-time Control authorization, and issue a fresh BrowserBroker grant scoped to the routine's allowed domains for each unattended fire.

items.title: Budgeted web research job contract with run-context cost attribution
items.summary: Package the existing search, scrape and browser-agent steps as one research run in the Model Plane: input {prompt, urls?, output schema?, max cost/credits, effort}, output {status, data, partial, partialSchemaValid, stopReason such as credit_limit_reached, creditsUsed}, with one active run per thread (409 thread_busy plus the running run id). items.whyItMatters: A predictable, budgeted research call gives other features, and any future external API user, one contract with partial results and a clear stop reason instead of stitching step-level agent routes together. items.title: External contract: full OpenAPI, then an audience-bound MCP server for Quarry and read-only connectors, SDK call-and-wait and a first no-code connector
items.summary: Generate the Quarry OpenAPI spec from the Rust request/response types with a CI route-coverage check (the checked-in spec lists about 46 paths against roughly 75 edge routes). Authenticate with OAuth from Control Plane auth-core (resource indicators, audience-bound tokens, protected-resource metadata, introspection cached by token hash), translate calls to Quarry edge and IC with a short-lived purpose-tagged service token, and write one metadata-only audit row per call. items.whyItMatters: Three of four reference sources expose MCP, and it is the AI-first distribution channel for external agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to use Verevon's web stack without leaking credentials. items.summary: Phase A (recommended): the Model Plane generates a declarative ExtractionProfile (selectors plus transforms, never arbitrary code) once per (org, url template, schema, prompt); Quarry validates and caches it per org (not under ZDR) and executes it deterministically on later scrapes, requesting regeneration when validation fails. items.title: One honest product identity: unified user-agent and optional signed agent traffic (Web Bot Auth style)
items.summary: Step 1 (S): replace the four inconsistent Quarry user-agent strings with one product UA, publish a matching bot-information page, and use the same token for robots matching. Step 2 (M): add optional Web Bot Auth style request signing (Ed25519 key per deployment, Signature-Agent header) for agent-originated traffic on the static, TLS and browser-egress paths, with the key held in Control Plane. Human-driven browsing stays unsigned unless policy says otherwise.
items.whyItMatters: Sites that allow verified agents will let governed Verevon traffic through instead of blocking it, which is the compliant alternative to stealth and fits the governance story. referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (Codex); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A feature gate requires an identifying agent header on every agent-originated request from the extension backend, and clients without support get an 'update required' refusal. Add autovacuum settings for the hot queue and event-history tables and move to scheduled index maintenance only once volume justifies it.

(b) Sign the Quarry browser, mcp-bridge and sandbox images in CI (cosign) and verify them at deploy or admission. (c) A usefulness event per web tool result (used, ignored, failed) from the Model Plane, aggregated per domain or provider in Ingestion and fed into capability-core scoring, with no content stored under ZDR.

items.title: Agent scaling bets: child browser subagents and WebMCP page tools (site playbooks and MCP exposure are covered by F-t2-043 and F-t2-064)
items.summary: Four independent, later-stage bets: URL-pattern-bound site playbooks (guidance only, never permissions) injected into browser observations and learned from successful run receipts; child browser runs with narrower child grants (read-only class, capped concurrency) spawned by a parent run; browser.observe/act exposed as an MCP tool behind the same broker grants and approvals; and WebMCP page-tool discovery executed as sensitive-class actions with one-shot approval.
items.whyItMatters: Playbooks raise success on common SaaS UIs, subagents give parallel research, MCP exposure lets external agents use Verevon's governed browser, and WebMCP positions Quarry for sites that publish typed tools.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (sixteen SKILL.md playbooks with autoInject {keywords, url}; subagent profiles with isolated browser state) and Codex (CDP WebMCP.enable per frame with toolsAdded/Removed events)
others: Aside outbound-only relay with allowlisted remote operations
Codex CI109 signed browser-access attestation for cloud agents
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Playbooks 2 of 3 (common); remote drivers 2 of 3 (common); subagents 1 of 3 (unique); WebMCP 1 of 3 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Playbooks: registry keyed by URL pattern or keywords, injected into the next observation header and marked as guidance. Subagents: spawn(profile, task) gives a new session with its own browser binding and a tool set filtered by profile, results returned as text. WebMCP: enable the domain per frame, keep a per-tab tool registry, expose tools as webmcp:<host>:<tool> with per-site permission and review.

verevonToday.gap: Quarry supports parallel runs and any authorised device can drive sessions (cloud-native, no relay needed). No URL-bound skills (grep of Model Plane found none), no WebMCP handling in Quarry crates, and neither child-grant fan-out from execution-core nor MCP exposure of browser tools is evidenced; these were not verified in code.

items.approach: Model Plane: URL-bound skills injected into observations (seed a few top sites, learn more via procedure compile in browser_procedure.rs); child browser runs with child grants and a per-org concurrency cap; MCP tool wrapper over the same grants. Ingestion Plane: discover WebMCP tools in observations and execute them as sensitive-class actions with fenced descriptions. Schedule each separately.
items.risks: Stale playbook selectors; cost explosion from subagents (cap concurrency per org); external clients must never obtain grants outside the user's ACL; page-defined tools are untrusted input.

items.title: Design spike only: drive the user's own signed-in Chrome through an attested extension backend, behind per-tab consent
items.summary: Only after the multi-backend work in R-t2-03-09: ship an MV3 extension with debugger permission and a relay to Quarry (native messaging or a hosted bridge) that registers a 'user_browser' BrowserBackend with isolated_egress=false and security_evidence=false. Allow it only for interactive (non-background) runs with explicit per-tab user consent, a visible indicator, and Quarry relaying and recording every action the Model proposes. || Write an ADR and prototype scope for an extension plus native-host bridge that lets the user's own Chrome/Edge profile act as a Quarry executor kind. To keep the Model-proposes/Quarry-executes rule, the extension would only run actions that Quarry has already validated against a BrowserBroker grant and would return receipts to Quarry; it must not take instructions from the Model Plane or the SPA directly. Do not start implementation until the connector-to-browser bridge and Quarry profile login hand-off have shipped.
items.whyItMatters: It is the only route to SSO-protected enterprise apps and the user's signed-in state without importing credentials, and it delivers the 'it uses my browser' experience that Codex offers. It is high value but conflicts with Verevon's governed-egress model, so it is a later, deliberate product decision. || Users want agents to use sites where they are already signed in, without re-authentication. It is an alternative to R-t2-10-01 for authenticated access, but it weakens the server-side containment that makes ZDR, egress proof and grants enforceable.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex native messaging host plus extension using chrome.debugger (codexbrowser-in-app-browser-010, SRC)
others: Codex browser plugin (Chrome extension plus Rust native messaging host bridged to the app server)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 4 sources (codex), unique || 1 of 4 sources for the extension and native-host pattern (Codex only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: MV3 extension with the debugger permission attaches chrome.debugger to tabs the user shares; a native messaging host (or hosted WebSocket bridge) relays CDP commands from the agent service; the extension enforces per-tab consent and shows an indicator. || Merged items add: Extension to native host over stdin/stdout; native host to app server over a local WebSocket or named pipe; the manifest pins extension ids and required protocol versions with explicit update-required errors; tab-context assets are written in bounded chunks.

Any bridge has to be designed around the rule that the browser client never receives CDP endpoints or Quarry tokens. || No extension or native host; all browsing is a remote leased Chromium in Quarry. This is deliberate and enforces ZDR, egress control and grants server-side.

items.approach: Spike, not build: measure how much of the need is already met by the secret bridge (F-t2-024) and takeover login into scoped profiles, then decide in an ADR. If pursued, it is one more backend in the multi-backend abstraction (F-t2-059) with its own reduced capability set, because it gives up egress containment, SSRF guarantees and ZDR evidence. || Source detail: [R-t2-03-12] Frontend Plane: extension and consent UI. Ingestion Plane: 'user_browser' BrowserBackend with capability flags set false for containment and ZDR evidence so policy can refuse it for ZDR and background runs; the Model proposes and Quarry relays and records; the Model Plane approval grants (sensitive actions) still apply. Treat as a separate product decision with security review before any build. || [R-t2-10-08] Frontend Plane (extension, distribution) plus Ingestion Plane (a new executor kind registered with Quarry) plus Model Plane (BrowserBroker grant). Start with an ADR; a prototype would register the extension as a lease provider attested by a device key, with egress proof and ZDR weaker than remote Chromium and clearly labelled.

items.risks: Loses egress containment and SSRF guarantees; ZDR evidence cannot be guaranteed; extension store review and enterprise rollout; prompt-injected pages act with the user's real sessions. || Exposes the user's full signed-in profile to agent actions; hard to audit; conflicts with Quarry executes and with ZDR/egress guarantees; extension permissions and store review burden.

waves.goal: Unblock and make safe: production browser grants, close ZDR/tenant leaks and ungated script, stop resource leaks and relaunches, ship the inline ScrapeOptions contract and file routing, plus S-sized reliability fixes. Includes phase 1 of F-t2-013 (takeover enforced in Quarry).

adrNeeded.topic: Web policy of record and tighten-only claims (org-core in Control Plane vs capability-core in Model Plane)
adrNeeded.why: Several items need one owner for disabled/allowed/forced capability policy that reaches Quarry only as signed claims (no cross-plane DB access). The consolidators left the owner open; Space access must never widen it.

adrNeeded.topic: Secret custody across planes for browser credential use
adrNeeded.why: integration-corev2 holds secrets, Quarry would resolve and fill them, and the Model must only ever see opaque references. This touches plane ownership, audit and ZDR (no secret material in receipts or telemetry).

adrNeeded.topic: Shared human+agent sessions: grant binding, control lease and human-session navigation policy
adrNeeded.why: Free human browsing needs a broker-defined navigation policy that is not a single-host allowlist, and co-browsing binds a Model run to a user lease. Both change what a grant means and must keep "the Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects".

adrNeeded.topic: ZDR semantics for caches, monitors, schedules, durable crawl and telemetry
adrNeeded.why: Monitors, URL caches, schedules and durable crawls all store content or fingerprints; the team must decide per feature whether ZDR means hash-only, inline-only or refused, and publish it as the ZDR capability matrix.

adrNeeded.topic: Anti-bot posture: honest identity vs stealth, robots override, proxy escalation
adrNeeded.why: Consolidated items conflict (delete stealth code vs wire it under policy). Verevon contracts forbid challenge bypass; the ADR should confirm the honest posture and what policy-gated escalation is allowed.

adrNeeded.topic: Script execution model: evaluate, scrape actions and code-mode vs one governed action per call
adrNeeded.why: Code-mode REPL and generated extractors are model-written programs; they fit only if every binding call is still validated and executed by Quarry with grants, caps and no raw mutating script by default.

adrNeeded.topic: External agent exposure (MCP server) and its auth model
adrNeeded.why: docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG defers MCP exposure; an MCP front needs audience-bound OAuth, delegation to Quarry and integration-corev2, and a ZDR-aware tool-call log. Owner decision required.

adrNeeded.topic: Run trace envelope and sharing: Model Plane run trace vs Application Plane projections and Space grants
adrNeeded.why: A canonical cross-plane trace envelope and live projections must not let a Space member see more than the owning plane ACL allows.

adrNeeded.topic: Automation owner for follow-ups and routines (Application Plane vs Model Plane routines)
adrNeeded.why: Completion-triggered follow-ups and scheduled/heartbeat agent runs need one owner and per-fire browser grants for unattended runs.

adrNeeded.topic: Browser execution substrate: shared Chromium pool vs per-session containers/VMs, remote providers and user-browser extension
adrNeeded.why: Isolation level, processor approval for remote providers and the egress-containment proof decide which backends may run agent sessions; the user-browser extension gives up containment and ZDR evidence.
